title: Faith Speaks, Grace and Glory Increase
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Context of Perseverance
subpoints: Paul and Timothy endure hardship without losing heart
Preaching the Word in season and out of season
Suffering does not equate to destruction or despair

outline.title: Faith Speaks
subpoints: The Old Testament pattern of faith and testimony
Christian speech is characterized by grace and consistency with faith

outline.title: Grace and Glory Increase
subpoints: Grace abounds through the spread of the Gospel
Thanksgiving to the glory of God is the ultimate goal
Resurrection hope sustains believers through affliction

summary:
In this sermon, Pastor Tito Lyro explores 2 Corinthians 4:1-15, focusing on the relationship between faith, speech, and the resulting increase of grace and glory. The message begins by acknowledging the reality of suffering for believers, noting that Paul and Timothy were hard-pressed, perplexed, and persecuted, yet they did not lose heart. This perseverance is rooted in the confidence that God is good and that the light of the Gospel continues to shine despite opposition.

The central thesis of the sermon is that faith speaks. Citing Psalm 116:10, the pastor argues that speaking always follows believing. God’s people have historically been a speaking people because they are a believing people. This principle is illustrated through the life of Paul and the daily interactions of believers, emphasizing that Christian speech should be seasoned with grace and consistent with the Gospel. The sermon highlights that believers are not ashamed of the Gospel because it is the power of God unto salvation.

Finally, the message concludes with the assurance that because faith speaks, grace and glory increase. The ultimate purpose of the ministry is for grace to spread through many, causing thanksgiving to abound to the glory of God. This hope is anchored in the resurrection, where the same God who raised Jesus will raise believers, ensuring that present afflictions are temporary compared to the eternal weight of glory to come.
